a small privileged class of people that were noble (high social rank) by birth
having absolute control over people as in autocratic rule
citizenship in a city, region or country

the act or ceremony of crowning a monarch; legal recognition of king or queen
a territory with clearly defined and internationally recognized borders and an independent government
the learned and shared way of life of a group of people, which includes the generally accepted customs, beliefs, and values

the theory that the monarch has received his or her right to rule from God rather than from the people

(French) literally, a person who has "migrated out"; often a political self-exile
a male monarch, usually the sovereign ruler of an empire or another type of imperial realm
the Age of Enlightenment; an eighteenth-century movement in European philosophy that advocated reason as the primary basis of authority
a social class (group) of people such as the noblemen or peasant class
a group of people with common racial and cultural traits such as language, religion, and customs
nationalism based on a shared common ethnic background
the political, social, and economic structure of medieval society that remained in parts of Europe into the 1700s
both Status and Non-Status Indians in Canada, as defined by Canadian laws

the key characteristics that people use to describe who they are
a theory or concept about the way in which society should be organized
belief in the primary importance of the individual and in the virtues of self-reliance and personal independence
(in English: people) the aboriginal people of Arctic Canada traditionally with a distinct territory, social structure, and language

the principle that a country's rulers should come only from old, established aristocratic families (noble people of high rank)
a political philosophy that all citizens should have government-guaranteed freedoms and equality
a monarch whose power has been limited by a constitution
language as a characteristic of identity
historically, the children of French fur traders and Cree women in the Prairies, and of English and Scottish traders and Dene women in the North
a king or queen (tsar or tsarina in Russia)
an independent (self-governing) nation with a population of two or more ethnic or cultural groups within clearly defined borders that are internationally recognized

a group of people who share a common culture with common customs, origins, history, language, and frequently religion
an independent (self-governing) nation within clearly defined borders that are internationally recognized.
the feelings people have in identifying with their nation

love and support for one's country
the point of view that is shaped by one's background and experiences

a political philosophy involving a conservative reaction to change, meaning that change should be stopped and things be put back to the way they were
to make changes for improvement to remove abuse and injustices; "reform a political system"

a sudden, extreme change in thinking and/or the way something is done
someone who supports the monarchy
a group of people of the same standing or rank in a society

the right to vote
